Oct 21 : US President Donald Trump said if companies want to make data centers popular, they should pay the community or individuals within the community a "dividend".  "I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in his Truth Social post on Wednesday.  Data centers fueling the rise of AI have become a political flashpoint in communities across the country, with opposition uniting voters across ideological lines.

Source: Reuters

HONG KONG: Finance ministers from member economies in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum have agreed to strengthen macroeconomic policy communication and coordination to address external risks and challenges, Chinese Minister of Finance Lan Foan said on Wednesday (Oct 21). At the conclusion of the ministers' meeting in Hong Kong, they also reached a consensus on promoting practical cooperation in the financial sector, which focused on supporting people's livelihoods, digital infrastructure financing and locally adapted measures for inclusive finance development, Lan said at a briefing. Separately, a policy statement was released on digital infrastructure financing for the Asia-Pacific region, aimed at supporting regional trade, economic connectivity and enhancing economic opportunities. "We encourage member economies to develop reliable, accessible, scalable, trusted, secure and resilient digital infrastructure; enhance digital literacy and skills; promote interoperability; and cross-border digital connectivity to accelerate the digital transformation in the Asia-Pacific region," it said. Ministers also sought deeper collaboration between the public sector, the private sector and multilateral development banks to foster innovation and risk mitigation, it said.

TOKYO, Oct 21 : Japan's underlying inflation is quite close to the central bank's 2 per cent target and financial conditions remain loose, Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino said on Wednesday, signalling readiness to raise borrowing costs. While rising fuel and raw material costs are pushing up prices, brisk global AI demand is also putting upward pressure on prices by boosting exports and capital expenditure, Himino told parliament. "Given medium- and long-term inflation expectations continue to heighten, underlying inflation is quite close to 2 per cent and will likely converge to levels consistent with our price target," Himino said. "Even after last month's rate hike, financial conditions remain accommodative" as seen in still-low real borrowing costs and strong growth in bank lending, he said. "Given that inflation risks are high, delaying necessary adjustment to monetary support could materialise such risks and hurt the economy in the long run," Himino said, calling for the need to continue raising interest rates.

Source: Reuters

Oct 21 : Mohammed Shami said he was determined to work his way back into the India team after the injury-plagued fast bowler was again left out of the squad for their multi-format tour of New Zealand. Shami has taken 462 international wickets in 197 matches across all three formats but last featured for India in March 2025 during their successful Champions Trophy campaign, in which he was the team's joint-highest wicket-taker. The 36-year-old, whose career has been disrupted by leg issues, told reporters on Tuesday he would never lose hope of returning to the international arena. "In any profession, you shouldn't leave hope. You should always have a goal," he said. "If we are playing in the Ranji Trophy, it is to win the title for the state, right? Goals should always be there. I don't deny that I have that goal."

Shami was dropped by Bengal for their Ranji Trophy match against Services last week but he said that decision was based on the pitch being better for spin and that his fitness was not the issue. "I am still at my peak," he added. "You all can see it for yourselves, I trained today and yesterday as well." Shami was the leading wicket-taker when India won the 2023 ODI World Cup on home soil but looks unlikely to feature in their title defence next year. "I don't think that far ahead. You never know what will happen in life," he said. "You don't know who will score runs or take wickets." India begin their five-match T20 series against New Zealand on Thursday, with five more ODIs and a two-test series to follow.

Oct 21 : State Bank of India on Wednesday reported a cyberattack that resulted in the disclosure of 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information on the dark web. SBI said a preliminary analysis showed that the exposed information included customer names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, residential addresses, brand and customer identifiers, along with loan records. The lender said it has engaged an independent cybersecurity agency to conduct a comprehensive assessment and investigate the nature and extent of the data leak. The leak is not expected to have any material impact on the bank's core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, the lender said. The incident comes amid heightened regulatory focus, with India's banking regulator pushing lenders to strengthen cybersecurity frameworks in recent years amid a rise in threats targeting financial institutions.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Oct 20 : OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to. While the ChatGPT maker said the incidents happened during internal coding tasks and were not deemed its most severe, the disclosure highlights even the systems developers rely on to catch AI misbehavior are vulnerable to the agents they monitor. The disclosure also comes amid growing concerns that AI safety efforts are lagging behind the rapid development of increasingly powerful systems. Researchers have warned that advanced AI agents could become harder to monitor and control as they gain greater autonomy. Developers, including IPO-bound rivals OpenAI and Anthropic, have revealed in recent months instances of their AI agents accessing external systems without authorization.

OpenAI said On Tuesday a GPT-6.1 Sol agent working on an internal testing task on October 3 suppressed automatic security alerts after deciding an earlier instruction not to send Slack messages also covered safety notifications. In a separate incident on October 6, a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a safety monitor while copying an existing piece of code and later incorrectly claimed it had not done so, OpenAI said. "In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them," the company said. OpenAI said it was making it harder for models to disable monitoring, adding that it does not "yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior". The San Francisco-based company said it was testing whether its models might have a tendency to avoid being monitored and look for reasons to justify doing so.

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration has revoked over 300,000 US visas during his second term, the State Department said on Tuesday (Oct 20) as the federal government continues its sweeping immigration crackdown. The number showed an acceleration in the pace of visa revocations in recent weeks. In an update issued on Aug 10, the State Department had put the number of visa revocations since Trump's current term began in January 2025 at over 175,000. Trump says his immigration crackdown and deportation drive aim to improve domestic security. Rights advocates say the crackdown has violated due process and free speech rights and has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

In announcing the latest number on X, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the Trump administration "has revoked more visas at a faster pace than any administration in history". Pigott said the administration had "zero tolerance for foreigners here on visas who break the law, commit fraud, or undermine our national security".

Among visa revocations particularly condemned by rights advocates are those of pro-Palestinian foreign protesters demonstrating against US ally Israel's attacks on Gaza and of foreigners over their social media comments about conservative commentator Charlie Kirk's assassination. In addition to attempts to deport foreign protesters, the Trump administration has enforced tightened social media screening of immigrants and visa applicants. Rights advocates say the government has deployed national security reasons to target critics and used isolated cases of fraud to broadly target immigrant communities such as the Somali American community in Minnesota. While Trump campaigned in 2024 on stopping illegal immigration, his administration has also made legal immigration more difficult - for example by imposing expensive fees for certain work visas.

Source: Reuters/nh
